logline: A Philadelphia couple grieving their dead infant son hire a mysterious nanny to care for a lifelike reborn doll, and her arrival unleashes something neither grief nor reason can explain.

bollymeter.basis: 83% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 70 across 40 reviews. The Shyamalan-produced premiere season landed as a distinctive Apple TV+ flagship - atmospheric, slow-burn, and purposefully strange.

pull_quotes.text: Servant is an unfocused yet ultimately creepy good time with enough character and charm to keep its hazy nightmare from lulling you to sleep.

seasons.review_body: Servant launched November 28, 2019 as one of Apple TV+'s flagship originals, earning 83% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 70 across 40 reviews. The M. Night Shyamalan-produced psychological thriller made immediate use of its claustrophobic single-location premise - a Philadelphia townhouse where grief, denial, and something uncanny coexist in every room. Paste Magazine called it 'an unfocused yet ultimately creepy good time with enough character and charm to keep its hazy nightmare from lulling you to sleep.' New York Magazine's Vulture likened it to 'a Black Mirror installment stretched into ten half-hour parts.' Lauren Ambrose's performance as Dorothy Turner anchored the show's surrealist tension. The dread was genuinely effective for viewers who surrendered to its pace.

episode_reviews.title: Reborn
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the Turners' opulent Philadelphia home, Dorothy's reborn doll, and the arrival of Leanne Grayson with extraordinary efficiency. The show's tonal commitment to dread over explanation is announced immediately.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first moment the doll's status becomes ambiguous - the series' central question crystallised in a single, unsettling image.

bollymeter.basis: 88% on Rotten Tomatoes. Season 2 deepened Leanne's backstory and pushed the supernatural stakes higher. Entertainment Weekly noted it building steadily toward 'another chaotic and awful reckoning.'

pull_quotes.text: The sophomore season seems to be building steadily toward another chaotic and awful reckoning with Leanne.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived in January 2021 to 88% on Rotten Tomatoes as the show expanded Leanne Grayson's origins and introduced the Church of the Lesser Saints as a structural threat. Entertainment Weekly noted the season 'seems to be building steadily toward another chaotic and awful reckoning with Leanne.' The show's willingness to delay explanation in favour of atmosphere continued to divide audiences, but the performances solidified - particularly Nell Tiger Free's increasingly multivalent portrayal of Leanne, who shifted across the season from apparent victim to something considerably more dangerous. The Philadelphia townhouse remained the show's primary setting and best character, its rooms carrying different weight in every scene.
seasons.season_over_season: Expands the mythology around Leanne's origins while intensifying the confined dread of the townhouse setting.

bollymeter.basis: 91% on Rotten Tomatoes. Season 3 is the show's strongest dramatic season - the Church threat becomes concrete and the Turner marriage fractures under supernatural and psychological pressure simultaneously.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 was Servant's critical high-water mark at 91% on Rotten Tomatoes - the point where the show's slow-burn construction paid off most coherently. The Church of the Lesser Saints' threat became visible and physical rather than implied, and the domestic dynamic between Dorothy, Sean, and Leanne reached its most overtly adversarial configuration. Season 3's dramatic clarity rewarded patience with the mystery-box format. The show was still in no hurry, but its decisions now felt purposeful rather than evasive. The 90% overall Metacritic series score across 40 reviews partly reflects how Season 3 raised the critical floor across the run.
seasons.season_over_season: The strongest season structurally - the season-long patience pays off with more coherent dramatic momentum.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes for the final season. The conclusion resolved the show's central mystery with the same elliptical confidence that had characterised the run from the start.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 earned a perfect 100% on Rotten Tomatoes as the show's final run, airing January 2023. The finale resolved its core questions with the same elliptical confidence the show had always displayed - explanation was never the point. The final season concerned itself with consequence and the psychological cost of what the Turners had suppressed and survived. The overall series Rotten Tomatoes score of 90% across 114 reviews reflects a show that grew into its ambitions over four seasons. The 79% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes and the Metacritic series score of 70 across 40 reviews capture a show that rewarded patience and polarised those who preferred faster answers.
seasons.season_over_season: An earned conclusion - resolves the central mystery while honouring the show's refusal to over-explain.
